steps.python_approach: pd.read_csv(csv_path) with default RangeIndex (raw 0-based row positions kept). Apply make.names to column names (no-op here). For every text column selected with pd.api.types.is_string_dtype, strip surrounding single/double quote characters so values match R's quote handling. No rows dropped, no sorting or reset_index.
np.minimum on each column, in R order, before any feature engineering.
Map Area to 1-based position in its sorted unique levels (A..F -> 1..6) as integer.
np.minimum(VehPower, 9) converted to string label; dummies built later from captured xlevels ['4'..'9'], reference '4'.
Explicit vectorised mapping: VehAge==0 -> '1', 1..10 -> '2', 11..110 -> '3', otherwise NaN (as R's out-of-range matrix index). Level order from xlevels ['2','1','3'].

Explicit mapping with band edges 18-20,21-25,26-30,31-40,41-50,51-70,71-100 -> '1'..'7', outside 18..100 -> NaN. Level order from xlevels ['5','1','2','3','4','6','7']. DrivAge is a protected attribute: reproduced faithfully and flagged.
np.minimum(BonusMalus,150) as integer; np.log(Density) as float.

Keep as cleaned strings; treatment dummies named '<var><level>' built explicitly against the captured xlevels (reference = first xlevel). Values not in xlevels give NaN rows in the design (prediction NaN).

steps.python_approach: Not re-implemented. fit() receives the training rows chosen by the harness from the frozen R split; no RNG in the module.

steps.r_construct: model.matrix for the formula (intercept + treatment contrasts)
steps.python_approach: Design function builds columns in exactly meta.json term order: '(Intercept)'=1.0 first, then for each formula term either the numeric column or explicit 0/1 dummies for every non-reference captured level.

steps.r_construct: glm(..., data = learn, offset = log(Exposure), family = poisson())
steps.python_approach: numpy IRLS mirroring glm.fit for poisson/log: mustart = y + 0.1, eta = log(mustart), offset = log(Exposure); working response z = eta - offset + (y-mu)/mu, weights w = mu; weighted least squares via QR; deviance stop rule |dev-dev_old|/(|dev|+0.1) < 1e-8, maxit 25; standard errors from the R factor of the last iteration's weighted design (dispersion 1). Rows with NA in any model variable dropped from fitting (na.omit).

predict(result, df) = exp(X beta + log(Exposure)) using the same design function and captured levels (offset evaluated in newdata as predict.glm does); NaN wherever any input is missing or unmappable.
Return DataFrame(term, estimate, std_error) with term names exactly as R (meta.json terms).
